newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen steady in line with long-end rates.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen steady in line with long-end rates.

text.p: The key three-month Euroyen futures contract was steady in late morning trade on Tuesday in line with declines in rates at the longer end of the yield curve.
Key March was at 99.24 at 0206 GMT, up from 99.23 at Monday's settlement.
In the cash short-term market, the benchmark overnight call rate was most actively traded at 0.52 percent, unchanged from Monday but up from 0.48 percent a week ago.
The firmness in the call rate was purely technical and reflected banks' needs to roll over funds that matured today, traders said.

"There is absolutely no negative factor in the market, which is supporting Euroyen prices. However, it is psychologically difficult to buy them up as they are approaching record-high prices," said a European bank trader.
Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said on Saturday that he sees the Bank of Japan keeping an easy monetary stance for now.
Kubo told reporters that the BOJ governor had been saying that the central bank's monetary policy would be geared to putting the economy on a sure recovery track.
Three-month certificates of deposit were traded at 0.53 percent, a rate unchanged since September 3.
Banks remain interested in getting profits out of spread trading between short- and long-term instruments, traders said.
This is done by raising funds in the short end of the market and investing them in the long end, taking advantage of the positive yield curve, they said. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk 813-3432-8676
